issues.description: Check name, metadata, code, CHANGELOG, and PR title disagree on what is being verified (single vs multiple, plus undocumented MANUAL state)
issues.detail: The PR title and description describe 'compute_instance_multiple_network_interfaces' with PASS/FAIL semantics, but the directory, filename, class, metadata CheckID, and CHANGELOG entry all say 'compute_instance_single_network_interface', and the code introduces a third MANUAL outcome for GKE that metadata.json does not acknowledge. Pick one specification and make every artifact agree: align name across PR title, CHANGELOG, files, and class; either document MANUAL in metadata.json (and confirm the Check_Report contract supports it) or drop the MANUAL branch. As shipped, a reviewer cannot derive the check's behavior from its metadata, and downstream consumers searching for the documented CheckID will not find it.

issues.description: GKE detection by name-prefix string match is a bypassable heuristic, not an invariant
issues.detail: Classifying an instance as GKE-managed via instance.name.startswith('gke-') is a folk heuristic on a user-controllable string. Any operator can name a non-GKE VM 'gke-foo' and silently downgrade a FAIL to MANUAL, defeating the very property this check exists to enforce; conversely, real GKE node names can be customized. The authoritative signal lives in labels (goog-gke-node, goog-k8s-node-name), kube-env metadata, or managed-instance-group membership. Lift detection onto the Instance ADT (e.g. is_gke_managed derived once in compute_service from labels/metadata) and have the check read that field, or drop the MANUAL branch entirely and let users suppress findings the normal way.

issues.description: Zero-NIC branch silently reports PASS without stated invariant or test coverage
issues.detail: When interface_count == 0, report.status remains the default 'PASS' from the top of the loop while status_extended says 'has no network interfaces.' GCE instances must have at least one NIC, so this branch is unreachable for valid data — yet if it ever fires (a data-collection bug or API edge case), the check silently passes on an instance whose 'has exactly one NIC' postcondition is false. State the invariant on the Instance ADT and remove the branch, or set status to MANUAL/FAIL with a clear message; either way, no test exercises this branch today, so the contract is also under-tested.

issues.description: NetworkInterface ADT is anemic — drops accessConfigs/natIP and duplicates the existing public_ip representation
issues.detail: The new NetworkInterface model keeps only name, network, and subnetwork while _get_instances still derives a separate public_ip boolean by re-walking accessConfigs in the same loop. This creates two parallel representations of the same upstream object and forces future checks (per-NIC public IP, ip_forwarding, alias ranges, cross-VPC bridging) to re-parse the raw API. Extend NetworkInterface with access_configs/has_external_ip/networkIP/aliasIpRanges (and ideally stackType) and derive the instance-level public_ip from the list so the ADT is the single source of truth.

issues.description: network/subnetwork URLs are truncated to the last path segment, losing project/region context
issues.detail: interface.get('network', '').split('/')[-1] keeps only the final path component of the GCP self-link, discarding the project and region. Two 'default' networks in different projects become indistinguishable, which will mislead any future check that reasons about cross-project or cross-VPC bridging. Preserve the full self-link on the ADT (and derive the short name when rendering), or at minimum document the lossy transform as a postcondition on the field.

issues.description: Tests do not cover the zero-NIC branch
issues.detail: The check has three branches (==1, >1, else) but the test suite covers only one, two, three, four, and GKE-multi NICs. The else branch is reachable (the default network_interfaces value is []), produces user-visible status_extended, and is entirely unverified. Add a test for interface_count == 0, or remove the branch in favor of an asserted invariant on the Instance ADT.

issues.description: PR conflates a service-layer model change with a new check
issues.detail: The compute_service.py changes add a new NetworkInterface model and populate it inside _get_instances, while the check is added on top of that model in the same PR. Split into two patches: (1) add NetworkInterface to the Instance ADT with its own service-level tests covering field population, then (2) add the check on top. The current bundling means model reviewers approve the check and check reviewers approve the model, and both get incomplete coverage.

issues.description: interface_names computed unconditionally and status_extended assembled in three near-identical sites
issues.detail: interface_names = [nic.name for nic in instance.network_interfaces] is built for every instance regardless of which branch executes, and the same f-string status_extended pattern is rebuilt three times. The cost is trivial, but a literate comment stating the loop invariant (status starts PASS, is downgraded to FAIL or MANUAL based on interface_count; interface_names is purely for the human-readable message) would help the next reader, and consolidating to a single message-assembly site would make adding the next exemption a one-line change.

issues.description: Tests assert exact English status_extended strings and are mostly copy-paste
issues.detail: Several tests compare status_extended to exact sentences including punctuation; the behavior contract is the decision (PASS/FAIL/MANUAL given N interfaces), not the wording, so harmless copy edits will produce false negatives. Additionally, five tests differ only in the network_interfaces list and the expected outcome — that is a parametrize table, not five 50-line functions with identical mock.patch scaffolding. Convert to a data-driven table, assert on status + resource identity + counts, and leave the prose to a single golden test.

synthesis.summary: The panel reaches a clear consensus: the check ships with incoherent identity (name/metadata/CHANGELOG/PR title disagree on single vs multiple, and an undocumented MANUAL state appears only in code), and its GKE exemption is a bypassable name-prefix heuristic that any user can spoof by rename — a security predicate decided by a user-controlled string. The zero-NIC branch silently returns PASS without a stated invariant or test, and the new NetworkInterface ADT is anemic, duplicating the existing public_ip representation rather than subsuming it. Recommended actions before merge: align naming and CHANGELOG; specify or remove the MANUAL outcome; replace the GKE prefix check with an authoritative signal (labels/MIG membership) carried as a property on the Instance ADT; either remove the zero-NIC branch with an asserted invariant or handle it deliberately and test it; and enrich NetworkInterface so future per-NIC checks share one data shape.
